**Owner decisions (2026-11-09):**
- **#1 keyframe conflicts:** stable keyframe ids (model v3 with an upcast), replacing the `<param>@<time>` identity of the sub-project 4 spec (line ~1070); conflicts track the key, not its time; effect keys too.

- **#11 engine lifetime:** close an engine after 10 idle minutes (no subscribers, no commit lock, no long call), plus an explicit `project.close` RPC.

A split restricts each fade to each part (cleared where the window no longer reaches), so the envelope is unchanged at every time, including a cut inside a fade and overlapping fades (restricted independently, still multiplied); a fade a crossfade suppresses stays silent on the part that loses the transition. Trims, rolls and slides leave audio fields alone: fades are edge-anchored and the offset moves with its edge (so a roll at a split point inside a fade leaves a gain step; owner may revisit). Residual: each check and its operation are separate path lookups (a swap-and-restore between them goes unseen; closing it needs handle-based `openat` I/O). **#56** fixed (`7f4db730`, `48fff322`, `416a8ac1`): fin-text applies letter spacing itself (new `tracking.rs`), between shaping clusters only: never to the direction mark, a combining mark or after a line's last cluster. The line is then re-aligned at its tracked width with cosmic-text's rule (LTR/RTL; over-wide or unboxed lines unaligned). An LRM/RLM is inserted only when the line's own first strong character disagrees with the paragraph. **#57** fixed (`aaede981`, `416a8ac1`): new `ink.rs`; glyphs are placed by advances and shaping offsets, while line/word boxes, `width` and `overflow` come from scaled, positioned outline extents at the requested weight (colour/bitmap glyphs use their untracked advance; whitespace-only words get a zero-width box at the pen). Line breaking keeps a first word's start overhang from forcing one word per line; `layout.rs` ink-box contract and spec §5.6 updated. A negative left bearing at a left-aligned line start now reports overflow, as the ink contract requires (**owner decision 2026-11-12: keep the strict caption ink rule; no tolerance for left/right overhang**). Checked against the old code on the reel caption and single/multi-glyph cases, left/centre/right and boxed/unboxed: every line and word `x` moved by exactly the first glyph's left bearing (±1/64 px rounding at centre), and line breaks and baselines were identical, so placement is unchanged and only the reported boxes differ. `fin-testfonts` gained TestOverhang (W 50..750 on a 200 advance, J, U+0301, א, U+05B8) and TestColor; `FIN_TEXT_REVISION` 2→3; text corpus goldens re-blessed (new `overhang`, `combining-mark`, `tracking-right`, `tracking-rtl-center`, `tracking-marks`, `color-tracking`; generated `letter-spacing` x 3.75→1.875, real `chinese` baseline 67.75→67.91), wasm32-wasip1 hashes equal native; e2e reel goldens re-blessed (caption ink widths only, e.g. 45158→44698/64 px; line counts and heights unchanged). ### Follow-ups from 4B
- [ ] In-band fork resolution: a record kind chain resolution honours, so `CHAIN_FORK` needs no manual move-out (Decision 29; today: the manual procedure plus `fin project recover --import`)

- [ ] Conflict reasons: an undo whose clip is back already (re-created by a copy) is `ID_COLLISION`, where `ALREADY_PRESENT` would say it better (the undo planner does not judge origins)

Frame 10 maps to 10 (c2's removed range collapses to its start), our rebased slide puts c3's start at 9 without a shift, so the move lands inside c3, which the head only shifted (no change to blame). This is the documented *self relocation* limitation (positions map through shifts only, and a slide records none), not an engine bug; the oracle allowed it in equality (`self_relocates`) but not in refusals. As built: finisherd serves `FinRpcs` through its own NDJSON protocol (`protocol.ts`) instead of Effect's `makeProtocolSocketServer`: it caps inbound lines at 16 MiB (`FRAME_TOO_LARGE` to the request id read from the line's start, then close; the WebSocket's `maxPayload` is the cap plus 64 KiB), answers bad JSON, unknown frames, unknown tags, bad headers and payloads its schema refuses with `INVALID_REQUEST` (decoded here with the codec and parse options `RpcServer` uses, so the server's own decode never fails; a frame with no id to answer closes the connection), drops `x-fin-` headers and registers each connection with a `Link` (close, close after the reply, answer open requests then close). `connections.ts` records Effect 4.0.6's facts (client ids per protocol, so `Connections` is per transport; disconnects; where decoding fails); `ConnectionRegistry` sums the transports. `auth/handshake.ts` (`Handshake`: hello with `envId`, canonical endpoint, `serverNonce` and the proof only for a live credential with matching `env`/`endpoint`; one prove per hello; five failures close after the reply; `auth.fail` audited with `transport`), `auth/gate.ts` (`withAuthentication`: every RPC but `server.hello`/`auth.prove`; refusals counted in `rpc.stats`), `principal.ts`, contracts `auth.ts` (`PrincipalSchema`, `CredentialRefSchema`, the hello and `auth.prove` schemas, `PUBLIC_RPCS`, `defaultScopes`) and `scopes.ts` (`SCOPES`, `ScopeSchema`, `HUMAN_ONLY`; Task 5 adds the rules); `RPC_METHODS` += `auth.prove`; audit details gain `transport`. The WebSocket's connections start as `local` (its bearer token is a file of the user's, like `local.key`) until Task 6

- [x] Task 11: native Windows pipe listener. As built: `crates/fin-node/src/{pipe_win, pipe_loop, pipe_io, pipe_sec}.rs` (napi-free, Windows only) and `pipe_server.rs` (napi `PipeServer`; `PIPE_UNSUPPORTED` elsewhere). One thread owns every instance and one I/O completion port: overlapped `ConnectNamedPipe`, one pulled read (≤ 64 KiB) per connection, writes, and posted commands. The first instance (`FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE`, else `PIPE_SQUATTED`, exit 1) is an *anchor*: disconnected at once and kept until shutdown, it takes no client, keeps the name held while every other instance closes, and holds `WRITE_OWNER`, which Windows refuses to every later instance (found on the host) and `allow` needs. Instances: byte mode, `PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS`, `D:P(A;;GA;;;<user>)(A;;GA;;;SY)`; at most 64 client instances (`maxConnections`, the anchor is one more). Deviations from Decision 38: an allowed SID gets `0x12008b` (`FILE_GENERIC_READ | FILE_WRITE_DATA`), not `GRGW`, because `FILE_APPEND_DATA` is `FILE_CREATE_PIPE_INSTANCE` and would let a sandbox host the pipe; once any SID is allowed the descriptor carries `S:(ML;;NW;;;LW)` (an AppContainer runs at low integrity), and the peer check refuses every client that is not this user (or an allowed SID), and every low-integrity one that is not an allowed container. A client is checked from `GetNamedPipeClientProcessId` and its token (user, integrity, AppContainer) before its first byte; a refused one is disconnected and audited `auth.fail {credentialKind: pipe, reason: peer|unidentified, peer}`. Close is graceful (writes finish, then the handle closes once `FilePipeLocalInformation` shows the client read everything, it left, or 2 s passed), so `Link.terminate` reaches pipe clients. `apps/finisherd/src/pipe.ts`: each connection is a `PipeStream` (`Duplex`: pulled reads, `_writev` batching) that `NodeSocket.fromDuplex` makes a `Socket`, so the protocol (frame cap before decode, `INVALID_REQUEST`, `Link`) is the socket's; `ConnectionPeer` carries `{pid, sid}` into `Connections.peer` and the handshake's `auth.fail` rows (contracts: `peer` joins `address` in the auth-failure and pairing details). `transport.ts` `makeLocalServer` (Windows: the pipe; elsewhere the Unix socket); `claimSocketPath` does nothing on Windows. `fin` opens the pipe itself (`crates/fin/src/pipe_client.rs`): `GENERIC_READ | FILE_WRITE_DATA` with `SECURITY_SQOS_PRESENT | SECURITY_IDENTIFICATION` (`interprocess` connected at the impersonation level, so a squatter could act as the user), waiting on `ERROR_PIPE_BUSY`. Tests: `crates/fin-node/tests/pipe_server.rs` (Windows: squatting, `FILE_PIPE_REJECT_REMOTE_CLIENTS` read back, DACL read back, a deny-only-user token refused, peers, graceful close of 1 MiB, cap, shutdown, a real AppContainer refused, then allowed); `apps/finisherd/test/pipe.test.ts` (a fake native listener on every platform; the real one and a real finisherd on Windows)

Review of Task 7 (fixed before the commit): **B1** nonces are one per fixed 5-minute window of the clock (accepted until the start of window `e + 2`, exactly when their `jti`s are forgotten; a clock running backwards brings no window back), where lazy rotation had let a nonce outlive its replay memory by up to 5 minutes; **S2** `DpopCheck.knownKey`: a proof's `jti` is remembered only for a key the server knows (a live device's or a pending pairing's, Tasks 8–9), so made-up keys cannot fill the replay cache, and expired entries are dropped from the front of the cache, not by a full scan; **S3** canonical coordinates only (32 bytes in exactly 43 characters), so one key has one thumbprint; `htu` must be a string and `htm` is compared exactly. nothing is recorded when no server is reachable in time; gate: `DO_NOT_TRACK` (not empty/`0`/`false`) or `FIN_DIAGNOSTICS=off` in fin's env, or `finisherd.json` `diagnostics.enabled=false`; `FIN_SERVER` skips the file so fin sends and the server gates; name and flags from the clap parse (`describe`, long flag names that came from the command line, through `CLI_COMMANDS`/`CLI_FLAGS`, else `other`), `argsHash` = the write's command-input hash (`Tx.argsHash`'s, so it joins the commit's intent) else the canonical hash of the parse (command, flags sorted with their values, positionals in order), unkeyed `blake3:` on the wire; a suspended journal is `JOURNAL_UNAVAILABLE` with a `fix` by reason); `purge`, `project` and `consent` refuse `--dry-run` (USAGE); `export` streams JSONL pages by `next` (≤1000), `--since` takes `YYYY-MM-DD`, RFC 3339 `Z` or epoch ms; - [x] Task 4: the walker (parallel reads, timeouts, batches, polls, the test overlay). As built: `walk(src: Arc<dyn Source>, mode, &WalkOpts, sink, &CancelToken) -> Result<WalkSummary, WalkError>` (an `Arc`, not `&dyn`, so a read thread stuck past its deadline can be left behind); breadth-first by depth then raw chain, reads on up to `threads` lazily started threads, finished listings held in a window of `4 × threads` until every earlier directory is emitted, so batches are identical whatever the thread count. `WalkMode::Full {generation, known?}` (`gen` is reserved in edition 2024; `known` = the catalog's directories, the generated `KnownDir {dir, mtimeNs, entries, listedGen, mountRoot}` lines of `in/dirs.ndjson`, read by `KnownDirs::from_ndjson`; pass it on **every** full scan: it carries the mount and empty-suspect rules, and listings with `listedGen == generation` are skipped but descended), `Dirs {dirs, known?}` (exactly the given directories, minus excluded ones; with `known`, also subdirectories they report that the catalog does not know, e.g. a tree moved in), `Poll {known}` (known children re-stat'ed from the parent's handle with `Source::stat_child`; a known leaf costs one stat and no open; re-listed when the mtime changed, a known child vanished or is no longer a directory; new directories listed recursively; the root's own mtime by `Source::dir_mtime`). `Source` gained provided methods `read_dir_with(dir, progress)` (Linux: after the names and each `statx`; macOS: per `getattrlistbulk` buffer), `stat_child` (Linux `statx`, macOS `fstatat(AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)`; default lists the parent) and `dir_mtime` (default `None`: re-list); Task 3's Windows source should override all three. `Timing {firstStat 60 s, entry 30 s, flush 5 s}` (`flush`: a non-empty batch goes out at least that often). The first stat runs on its own thread (cancellable) and is judged by `classify_root` against `WalkOpts.stored`; offline, a known root with entries listing empty (`ROOT_EMPTY_SUSPECT`, in every mode, not only full scans), a failed or timed-out root listing, or as many stuck threads as `threads` end the walk with `WalkError::Offline(Box<RootState>)` (`.offline()`) before or between batches. A step-less read past `entry` gives `DirDone {complete: false, code: TIMEOUT}`; other not-descended directories get `CLOUD_ONLY` (placeholder), `AUTOMOUNT`, `ROOT_UNMOUNTED` (known mount root that is no longer one) or the open/listing error code; a listing that drops from N > 0 (known) to 0 is `DIR_EMPTY_SUSPECT` and incomplete. Batches ≤ `batch_entries` (4,096) entries + `DirDone`s and ≤ `batch_bytes` (8 MiB, estimated from above); a listing's `DirDone` lands with its last entry; `seq` from 0 per walk; a cancel stops within one batch; a sink error is `WalkError::Stopped`. As built: `fin-codecs::{config, registry, hung}` and `testing/fake.rs`. `ProbeResult {decoders, encoders}` of `DecoderBackend`/`EncoderBackend` trait objects (`software_only()` = dav1d + SVT-AV1 until Task 8; `capabilities()` derives the v1 table from it); candidates (decode and encode) hardware first, then by class (os, gpu, software, plugin), and only those on the session's adapter when both name one; encode candidates are then filtered by `encoder_allowed`; a candidate that fails to open gives way (noted `openFailed`). `EncoderBackend::open` takes an `OpenToken` only fin-codecs can make, so nothing outside opens an encoder past the policy. `EncoderSession` opens and drives each encoder on its own thread: hung when opening it or one call into it passes the deadline (`max(2 s, 120 frame durations)`; the clock covers the call, not a whole flush), when it holds `HUNG_FRAMES` (300) frames without producing a packet (counted on its thread), or when nothing comes after `finish` within the deadline; the hung thread is detached (it drops its encoder; events are unbounded so it never blocks), the next allowed candidate opens and `send`/`receive` answer `Restart` (the caller resends from frame 0, `fixture::encode_all` shows how); the second hang, or one with no candidate left, is `ENCODER_HUNG {backend, adapter}` (exit 5 in `fin` and `finisherd`). One packet per frame is checked at the end (`ENCODE_FAILED` otherwise). `fin-container` `VideoTrack.params: CodecParams {codec, fourcc, profile, level, bitDepth, chroma}`; `fin-media` `Profile::of`. Compositor: NV12 (R8 + RG8) and P010 (R16Uint + RG16Uint, no optional features) ingest on the reference and the GPU, I420 path bit-identical; `nv12_and_p010_ingest_match_reference` max |Δ| 1, PSNR ≥ 60.8 dB (run on SwiftShader Vulkan: this host has no lavapipe). `open_av1_encoder` is crate-private and in the call-site gate.     - [x] Task 12: WebM/Matroska demux under limits, with a fuzz target. As built: `fin-container` `demux/webm/{mod,ebml,segment,cluster,cues,codec_private}.rs`; `Demuxer::open` sends a file that starts with the EBML magic there, and it answers the same `VideoTrack` (`params` included), `AudioTrack`, `SampleTable` and `MediaInfo` as MP4 (`ContainerKind` gains `webm`, `matroska` from the `DocType`; another `DocType`, an EBML read version over 1 or a Matroska one over 4 is `UNSUPPORTED_CONTAINER`). Limits: an element is a box (ids ≤ 4 bytes, sizes ≤ 8, each size checked against the bytes its parent has left, nesting against `maxDepth`, a body read whole only within `maxBoxBytes`, unknown sizes only for `Segment` and `Cluster`: an unknown-sized cluster ends at the next Segment-level id); elements outside clusters and `Cues` count against `maxBoxes`, blocks inside clusters as samples (`maxSamples` per track, laced audio frames each, and at most the file's length in bytes, as MP4; `maxPresentedFrames` as MP4), cue points against `maxSamples` (a limit hit in `Cues` drops the cues, never the file); header reads go through a 64 KiB read-ahead window. Times: a video track's timescale is 10⁹ / gcd(10⁹, `TimestampScale`), so block times convert exactly (1 ms ticks give 1000; a scale of 33,333,333 ns gives 10⁹); decode times are the sorted presentation times (Matroska stores pts in decode order) less the largest reorder delay, so dts ≤ pts as in MP4; durations the gap to the next pts, the last frame's own `BlockDuration`, else `DefaultDuration`, else the gap before it (the same order for the last audio block); all time arithmetic checked (`MEDIA_CORRUPT`). VFR ignores one tick of rounding (33/34 ms frames at 30 fps are CFR); the nominal rate is `DefaultDuration`'s, else the mean (CFR) or most common (VFR) frame length's, snapped to a standard rate within 0.05 %. An audio track's timescale is its sampling rate, a laced block's span is divided between its frames; priming is the `OpusHead` pre-skip, else `CodecDelay`; padding the last block's `DiscardPadding`. Blocks: `SimpleBlock` (keyframe flag) and `BlockGroup` (key without a `ReferenceBlock`); video lacing is `UNSUPPORTED_CONTAINER`, an empty video frame, an empty laced frame (5 bytes of fixed lacing would make 256 samples) or a lacing that declares more bytes than its block `MEDIA_CORRUPT`. `CodecPrivate`: `V_AV1` is `av1C`, `V_VP9` feature records become a `vpcC` (profile from the bit depth and subsampling when absent), `V_MPEG4/ISO/AVC`/`V_MPEGH/ISO/HEVC` carry `avcC`/`hvcC`, `A_OPUS` `OpusHead` becomes `dOps`; other codecs demux with their ISOBMFF type (`mp4a`, `fLaC`, …) or `mkvv`/`mkva` and `Other` config. `Colour` → colour tags (over the codec record's), siting, `MaxCLL`/`MaxFALL` and the mastering display (mdcv units); `DisplayWidth`/`DisplayHeight` in pixels → pixel aspect; `ContentEncodings` on the video or audio track → `UNSUPPORTED_CONTAINER {format, reason: contentEncoding}` (other tracks are only listed in `ignored`); a `ProjectionType` other than 0, or a pose, → `UNSUPPORTED_TRANSFORM {projectionType}`. `fin-probe` dispatches the EBML magic to `fin-container` and keeps the container's `reason`; **`PROBE_VERSION` 2** (WebM was refused at 1; the finisherd library tests now read `libraryProbeVersion()`). Test-only writer `fin-container::testing::webm_writer` (feature `testing`); fuzz target `crates/fin-container/fuzz/fuzz_targets/webm.rs` (prepends the EBML magic when missing; no new dependency, so its `Cargo.lock` is unchanged and `--locked` builds), seeds from `fuzz_seeds <demux dir> <webm dir>`, nightly runs it 60 s. Tests: `fin-container/tests/webm.rs` (28 after the review fixes: the plan's `vfr_block_timestamps`, `cues_and_scan_agree`, `unknown_size_cluster`, `content_encoding_refused`, hostile sizes past the parent, a 2⁵⁶ − 2 size, depth, lacing over the block, times that overflow, counts, plus lacing, block groups, B-frame order, colour/HDR, projection, VP9, doc types, every truncation and a mutation sweep, `FIN_MUTATIONS` (200 k clean)); `fin-codecs/tests/webm.rs` (`av1_in_webm_decodes_like_mp4`: SVT-AV1 packets in both containers decode to identical planes in order and backwards; VP9 demuxes and is `CODEC_UNAVAILABLE` with the software probe, Decision 16); `fin-probe/tests/media.rs` `webm_probes_by_its_magic`. Fuzz (Linux x64, stable with `RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP=1`, built with `cargo fuzz build -s none`'s flags because `cargo-fuzz` is not installed on this host): `webm` 3 × 60 s, 2.17 M, 2.03 M and (on the final code) 2.59 M runs, no finding; `demux` 60 s with the webm seeds added, 3.54 M runs, no finding. **Deviations:** the cluster scan always runs (the table needs every block): `Cues` are read under the limits and checked against it, and add sync points only when the track flags no keyframe at all (a frame a cue names becomes a keyframe, so a file whose muxer left the flags unset still seeks; a cue naming no scanned cluster or frame is ignored) instead of replacing the scan; `av1_in_webm_decodes_like_mp4` lives in `fin-codecs/tests/webm.rs`, not `fin-container/tests/webm.rs` (a dev-dependency of `fin-container` on `fin-codecs` would be a cycle and build dav1d/SVT-AV1 for every container test); the 6A `not_an_mp4_is_unsupported` case for the EBML magic now expects `MEDIA_CORRUPT` (a cut-short Matroska header); `limits.rs` gained documentation only (no new field). The response is a series of 1 MiB reads; the first comes before the headers (a file that does not open is a 404, never half an answer); a reader that takes nothing for 60 s is cut off.   - **Behaviour (17/17 checks pass, `tough-check.log`):** `ExpirationEnforcement::Unsafe` loads an expired repository and still refuses a bad timestamp signature, an unsigned body edit, a lower timestamp version, a lower snapshot version, a wrong target hash and a target over its signed length (`Safe` refuses the expired timestamp). Root chain 1→2→3 with root-key rotations: killed when `3.root.json` is fetched, the datastore holds root 2; resuming from it reaches root 3. Fast-forward recovery: a timestamp-key rotation deletes the trusted `timestamp.json` and `snapshot.json`, and timestamp v3 signed by the new key is accepted after v10 (without a rotation v3 is `OlderMetadata`).
  - **Gaps `fin-registry::tuf` must cover (Tasks 4a/4b):** (1) `tough`'s datastore writes are not atomic (`tokio::fs::write`, no temp/rename or fsync; `root.json` is removed, then written), and it writes `timestamp.json` before the snapshot verifies (and so on down the chain): give `tough` a scratch datastore per refresh seeded with copies of the trusted set, and promote the result temp-then-rename only after `load()` succeeds. (2) `tough` takes the trusted root from the caller, never from its datastore, and stores it re-serialised (1,787 bytes for a 2,391-byte root): keep our own `<n>.root.json` chain from the raw fetched bytes; the `Transport` adapter, when asked for `<n+1>.root.json`, first saves the `<n>.root.json` it served (verified by then), temp then rename. (3) Any transport error on `<n+1>.root.json` ends the root walk as "no newer root": the fs transport returns `FileNotFound` only for a missing file, and the adapter fails the refresh after any other error on a root. (4) When a saved root rotates the timestamp or snapshot keys, delete our trusted timestamp and snapshot in the same step (`tough` compares only with the root passed in). (5) `tough` reads the wall clock and writes `latest_known_time.json` (`SystemTimeSteppedBackward`): do not seed it into the scratch datastore; always load with `Unsafe` and apply both `strict` and `relaxed` expiry with the injected `Clock`. (6) Size caps: `Limits` has root, timestamp and snapshot caps and `max_root_updates` (set 32), but a role whose length the snapshot lists is read up to that length, so the adapter enforces Decision 15's per-file caps by name; the ≤ 500 delegations cap is ours

Pass 1 reads only the central directory: duplicate central-directory names (`zip` keeps one entry per name, so a second one would be invisible here), entry count, UTF-8 names (non-ASCII needs the UTF-8 flag), stored or deflate and not encrypted, regular files and directories only, the name rules, declared bytes ≤ 512 MiB, ratio ≤ 200:1 per entry, a root `finisher-plugin.json` ≤ 256 KiB. Name rules (`check_path`, `check_component`): empty, `.`/`..`, leading `/`, `\`, NUL and control characters, `:` and Windows' other forbidden characters, reserved device names in any case and with any extension (CON… CLOCK$, COM0–9 and ¹²³, LPT likewise), trailing dot or space, components > 255 bytes, paths > 1,024, not NFC, case-folded duplicates (lower and upper case, files and directories alike), a file used as a directory. `tree_hash(root)` = BLAKE3 over sorted `path \0 class \0 sha256`, class `x` for the owner-execute bit (always `f` on Windows), empty directories add nothing. `pack(src, executables, out)` → `PackInfo {bytes, sha256, entries, tree_hash}`: files only, sorted, deflate level 6, DOS epoch, made by Unix (the `zip` writer otherwise writes DOS on Windows), 0644/0755 from the list, no extra fields; refuses what the reader would. Errors `{code, message, details}`: `PACKAGE_UNSAFE {entry, reason}`, `PACKAGE_TOO_LARGE {reason, limit, got}`, `PLUGIN_MANIFEST_INVALID {path, reason: missing|schema}`, `MANIFEST_TOO_LARGE`, `IO_ERROR`. As built: a lying declared size is caught by `zip` itself (`corrupt`) before the reader's own count (`sizeMismatch`); the "hard link" case is a second entry of one path (zip has no hard links; tools that keep them write duplicates)

New key-ring folders (and the missing folders above them) and every private key file are created owner-only in the creating call: Unix 0700/0600; Windows `CreateDirectoryW`/`CreateFileW` with a protected DACL `O:<user>D:P(A;OICI;FA;;;<user>)(A;OICI;FA;;;SY)` (files without `OICI`), nothing inherited, so a drive root's Authenticated Users/Users ACEs never reach a key, even before the rename. `SYSTEM` is granted: it is the OS and can read any file already, and services that run as it without backup semantics (VSS-based Windows Backup/File History, Defender, backup agents) would otherwise fail; Administrators are not granted. Loading is ssh-style on both OSes: `RepoBuilder::open`, every ring write and every ring key read check the ring folder, and `SigningKey::read` (ring keys, `--root-keys`, `--key`, `--new`) checks the file; anyone else reaching it is `KEY_UNPROTECTED {path, problems}` (exit 3) with `fix` = the `chmod 700`/`chmod 600` or `icacls` commands (`/setowner`, `/grant:r` user and SYSTEM, `/inheritance:r`, `/remove:g` explicit grants) and a message to rotate keys others may have read. Unix refuses any group/other bit (a `mkdir`-made 0755 ring is now refused, with `chmod 700`); Windows accepts owner = user, SYSTEM or Administrators and allow ACEs for those plus `CREATOR OWNER`/`OWNER RIGHTS` (as OpenSSH for Windows does; a ring under the profile passes), and refuses a NULL DACL (FAT/exFAT) or any other SID with non-zero access. `EditorError` gains `fix`. windows-sys 0.61 (already in the tree via tempfile) added to fin-registry with features only. As built: `fin-sandbox-exec` no longer `exec`s the program on Linux: `fin_sandbox::linux::reaper` makes it a child subreaper with a parent-death signal (`SIGRTMIN`, checked against `getppid` because the kernel sends it on the parent thread's exit), forks, and confines the child (own process group, session cgroup, signal mask restored, sockets hidden, Landlock, `RLIMIT_NOFILE`, death signal `SIGKILL`, `exec`); the unconfined launcher forwards `TERM`/`INT`/`QUIT`/`USR1`/`USR2`/`WINCH`/`CONT`/`ALRM`/`TSTP`/`TTIN`/`TTOU` to the program's group and, when the program exits, on `SIGHUP` and when its parent dies, kills the group, `cgroup.kill`s the session cgroup and kills each child until none is left, then exits with the program's code or re-raises its signal. Optional cgroup layer: `<own>/fin-session-<pid>` where the launcher's cgroup v2 is writable, has `cgroup.kill` and holds only its parent and the parent's children (`FIN_CGROUPS=off` skips it). `finisherd` `agent/sandbox.ts`: a `SIGKILL` of a process under the Linux launcher becomes `SIGHUP`, then `SIGKILL` of its group after `REAP_GRACE_MS` (2 s). A CLI that refreshes its token by writing a temporary file and renaming it over the store would, through the link, replace the link in `provider/` with a private copy (the shared store keeps the stale token and the next session signs in again), and where the profile refuses the rename (Seatbelt grants the file, not its directory) the refresh fails outright. Counters per plugin id (`EgressCounters`: requests, completed, denied, notHttps, privateAddress, secretMissing, rateLimited, tooLarge, timeouts, failed, redirects followed/returned, bytes in/out) through `PluginHost.egress.stats()` for Task 15. ## Windows run follow-ups (2026-11-08, `xwin-fixes`)

- [x] 4A: `fin` tests fail `ENGINE_BUSY {operation: "backup (auto)"}` (exit 5) on Windows when `cargo test -p fin` runs alone: the first-open daily backup holds the engine while parallel tests write, and `VACUUM INTO` plus fsync is slower there. A user's first command after a start can meet the same; ties to the 4A follow-up "the store mutex across folder I/O" (take the backup outside the engine's lock, or let writes wait for it)
  - Fixed (2026-11-08, `fin-node::auto`, spec §3.8/§3.10): automatic work starts only after 30 s with no short call (or 10 min after it fell due); the daily backup runs off the store on its own connection and thread (a WAL snapshot; `quick_check` before the no-replace rename; cancelled by any long call and retaken later); compaction runs one step per tick under the mutex. Neither takes the store out, so neither can cause `ENGINE_BUSY`. The test-build default that turned automatic work off (`setAutoWorkForTest`) is gone; tests set the quiet time (`setAutoIdleForTest`) where they need the work to run. New tests: 50 short calls during a backup due at open (vitest), a long call cancelling a running backup, the quiet-engine rule, and fin-store's `backup_job` (commits during the copy, cancels, truncated files, a process killed mid-backup). To re-check on Windows: `cargo test -p fin` alone

## Load-sensitive timing tests (patches for the owning branches)

Pattern: statistic + generous bound, strict bound only under `FIN_STRICT_TIMING=1`. Done for `engine.test.ts` "event loop keeps ticking" on sp4c-edit-breadth. The two below live on other branches and need the same treatment there.

- [ ] **`reader_never_waits_for_writer`** (`apps/finisherd/test/library/threads.test.ts`, home/sp5d-t7b; failed at 20.2 ms vs 20 ms). The writer spins 800 ms, so a reader that really waits for it takes about 700 ms. Replace `expect(Math.max(...times)).toBeLessThan(20)` with:
  ```ts
  const sorted = [...times].sort((a, b) => a - b);
  expect(sorted[Math.floor(sorted.length / 2)]).toBeLessThan(20); // median
  expect(sorted.filter((t) => t > 20).length).toBeLessThanOrEqual(2); // at most 2 of the 10 searches
  expect(sorted[sorted.length - 1]).toBeLessThan(process.env.FIN_STRICT_TIMING === "1" ? 20 : 250);
  ```
  Keep `expect(spinning).toBe(true)`. Prove with a mutant that makes `reader.search` take the writer's lock (it must fail on the 250 ms bound or the median).
- [x] **`diagnostics_project_never_then_default`** (`crates/fin/tests/cli_diagnostics_online.rs`, home/sp5a-t3, fn at ~539; times out under load). The positive waits go through `wait()` with a fixed 15 s deadline. Make the deadline `Duration::from_secs(env_secs("FIN_TEST_WAIT_SECS", 60))` (60 s default; `fn env_secs(k, d) -> u64 { std::env::var(k).ok().and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(d) }`). The failure branch stays: `assert!(want(&found), "timed out: ...")` after the deadline. Leave the 400 ms sleep before "no new ones are written" alone (it is a negative check and load only makes it weaker, never flaky); keep each `fin` call's own timeout, if any, scaled by the same value. Done on `sp5a-t5`: `wait()` takes `FIN_TEST_WAIT_SECS` (default 60 s); `fin` calls there have no timeout of their own to scale; the 400 ms negative check is unchanged.
